requirements.text: Students should be able to check the library catalogue anytime and see what's available in real-time.
Students should be able to handle borrowing or renewing items online without needing to come to the desk.
Students should be able to reserve study rooms online, choosing the date, time, and number of people.
The system must allow librarians to manage inventory effectively, including adding or updating catalogue items easily.
The system must automatically calculate overdue fines and enforce account restrictions for students with outstanding fines.
The new system must integrate smoothly with the existing student record system to verify enrollment before students can borrow items or book rooms.
The system must handle student data in compliance with GDPR.
Students should be able to see the capacity of each study room and any specific amenities available.
Students should be able to book for specific time slots and see which slots are already booked.
Students should receive confirmation emails or notifications after booking study rooms, as well as automated reminders.
Students should be able to cancel or change their bookings easily.
The study room booking process must be accessible for all students, including those with disabilities.
Students should be able to check the availability of books directly from the catalogue.
The system must provide a loan history and current loans overview for students, including due dates and outstanding fines.
The system must send automated email reminders before due dates for borrowed items.
Students with outstanding fines above a certain threshold must be blocked from making new loans or bookings until fines are cleared.
The interface must be user-friendly and easy to navigate for both students and staff.
Librarians must have tools to track the popularity of items and inform collection development decisions.
The system must automatically calculate fines based on a configurable daily rate for overdue items.
Students should have a clear view of their outstanding fines, including amounts owed and details about overdue items.
The system must allow students to track their payment history and fines paid.
The system must offer various payment methods for settling fines online.
Librarians must have access to reports showing fine revenue and trends over time.
The new system must integrate seamlessly with the university's student record system.
Data migration from the legacy system must be planned to avoid data loss.
The system must comply with GDPR regulations regarding the storage and processing of student data.
The project must adhere to budget constraints.
The system must adhere to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards.
Support and training must be provided to both students and staff for transitioning to the new system.
